learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn how to make your sentences colourful by using describing words and comparing things like a pro!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An adjective is a describing word! It paints a picture by giving more information about a noun or pronoun. It tells us what kind, how many, or which one, like a 'tall' tree or 'three' birds.
When we just want to describe one person or thing without comparing it to anyone else, we use the Positive Degree. For example, 'Rohan is a fast runner.'
When we compare exactly two people or things, we use the Comparative Degree. We usually add '-er' to the adjective or use 'more', like 'Rohan is faster than Amit.'

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏆 The Superlative Degree (The Ultimate Best or Worst)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: When we compare three or more things, we use the Superlative Degree to show the highest quality! We add '-est' or use 'most', like 'Rohan is the fastest runner in the class.'

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Great Animal Comparison
fun_activity.instructions: Pick three different animals (like a dog, a horse, and a cheetah) and write three sentences comparing their speeds using fast, faster, and fastest!

quick_recap: ⭐ Adjectives describe or modify nouns and pronouns.
⭐ The Positive degree describes one thing without comparison.
⭐ The Comparative degree compares two things, usually ending in -er.
⭐ The Superlative degree compares three or more things, usually ending in -est.
